chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Big bands, personalities and youth rebelling against the industry
summary: He says big bands didn't need to come back, personalities can be made quickly by whoever controls the industry, and he trusts young people to reject what is dictated.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Looking at the existing big bands and how difficult it is for practically everybody to survive --
Sustain.

-- yeah, to keep going, even though it seems trite to go over the same thing that people keep talking, 'Well, big bands are coming back and the same old thing. But it may be a different kind of a situation.
There has to be, because that line went out with World War II, when you think about it, big bands coming back.
Yeah.
There's no reason for opening it for discussion.
Of course.
Because that's like trying to determine
Yeah. But, you see, all these colleges and universities, of course, have these big band units.
Right.

And I was just looking at it and saying, well, certainly if just a small percentage of those bands would be able to form, like so many other bands have, and come out I think maybe part of the problem is that there are no personalities taking over the bands, like you folks have, Stan, Harry...
Do you know how quickly personalities can be developed?
Overnight.
Quicker than you can say good morning.
And do you know, I think that in this day and age of PR and everything else --
All you need is someone who controls the industry to say, 'Hey, good, make the next move.' That's all--
Why do you think that hasn't happened?
Why hasn't it happened?
Yeah.

Because they all imagine that they are producers of the world, that they and only they control the selling and buying and all this. And I have this much faith in youth music today, that they're not going to buy it and they're not going to take that kind of crap.
Sooner or later that they would rebel.
I have a feeling they're going to walk in and say, 'Hey, baby, move over.'
I see, I see what you're saying.
That's what I think it's going to take, Herb. And you're young enough, I would like for you to be involved in it.
I see what you're saying now, when you referred to it a few moments ago.
I would like for them to walk into the president of every major label and not-so-major label and say, 'Hey, we're better than that crap, and you'd better face it.' It has to be a positive attitude.
Right, right. But it has to be pretty pervasive, too.
That's right.
So there's a feeling, a movement, going.
Right.
Yeah, that's going to take some --
Well, it's nothing that can be done in 20 minutes.
No, no.
